newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Bank says Morocco economy grew 12 pct in '96 - MAP.
newsitem.headline: Bank says Morocco economy grew 12 pct in '96 - MAP.

text.p: The Moroccan economy grew by 12 percent in 1996, according to the annual report of the Moroccan Bank al-Maghrib (central bank), quoted by the official news agency MAP on Wednesday.
It quoted central bank governor Mohamed Seqat as saying that the year had been marked by very satisfying results on the economic and financial levels.
MAP said the governor made the remarks at the royal Skhirat Palace where he presented the bank's annual report to King Hassan.
"The rate of growth of the national economy in 1996 reached 12 percent," MAP said, quoting the report.
In May, Finance Minister Mohamed Kabbaj said Morocco's GDP was 11.8 percent in 1996 but expected to register zero growth in 1997 due mainly to a serious drop in agriculture output.

MAP quoted the governor as saying that agricultural production in 1996 had registered an exceptional improvement which had produced opportunities for work and increase income which had affected the whole of Morocco's economic sectors.
Catastrophic drought hit Morocco the previous year.

Increased supplies of foodstuffs had also particularly freed tensions playing on prices and brought a reduction in the trade balance deficit. MAP said the report showed inflation had fallen to three percent in 1996 from 6.1 percent the year before.

The governor also said that foreign currency income from tourism and Moroccan expatriates abroad had shown a marked improvement. The current account deficit on balance of payments had fallen to represent only 1.8 percent of Gross Domestic Product instead of 4.6 percent in the previous year, MAP said.
It added that the budgetary deficit had been brought down to three percent of GDP instead of 5.3 percent in the year before.
The treasury had covered almost all its financial needs by calling on the capital market, limiting its need to create money, MAP quoted the report as saying.
The report said the annual monetary mass growth registered at 6.6 percent conformed to the norm fixed at the start of the year with the aim of containing pressure on prices and the external account.

MAP quoted the governor as saying the national economy had also benefited from investments and external credits, while the balance of payments had registered an important surplus which favoured the increase of foreign reserves and stability in the dirham's exchange rate.

Moroccan authorities changed the country's fiscal year to run from July to June instead of January to December after a referendum in 1996. It was not clear from the MAP report whether the bank report covered January-December 1996 or July 1996 to June 1997.
Officials were not available to comment at the central bank.
